requirement: Show the final failure taxonomy, the definitions of each category, and how the categories were derived or manually classified.
evidence: 37 codes across 5 dimensions (A=10, B=10, C=8, D=4, E=5); every code has a definition, an inclusion rule and an explicit exclusion clause, and the loader refuses to start if any is missing.
location: taxonomy.v1.yaml (frozen v1.0, all 37 boundaries documented); report section 4 and 4.1-4.4 (tables 4.1-4.5); derivation narrative in section 4.5; application tab 'Taxonomy'.
closed_by: Derivation procedure written out as a numbered protocol (source reading -> open coding -> consolidation -> boundary tests -> freeze), with the source basis of each category dimension named.

requirement: Traceable examples from real datasets or logs for each taxonomy category.
evidence: 49 exemplars covering 10 of 10 categories; each row carries record id, repository, issue number, URL and the evidence span that produced the label.
location: taxonomy_exemplars.csv; report section 4.6 with the per-category table; application tab 'Taxonomy'.
closed_by: Exemplar selection rule with a demonstration score, so the examples chosen are the ones whose text states the definition, not merely the ones the labeller was confident about. Selection rule and its rationale are published with the table.

requirement: Explicit research questions RQ1..RQn (2-10), not only dashboard questions.
evidence: 10 numbered research questions, each with a rationale, required variables, method, and named output artefact. 9 use a chain of agents, 1 a single agent.
location: research_questions.yaml; report section 6; paper section 3; application tab 'Research questions'.
closed_by: Questions are declared in a machine-readable config that the orchestrator reads, so the reported results cannot drift from the declared questions.

requirement: State which research question uses a single agent, which uses multiple agents, and why.
evidence: Every one of the 10 questions declares agent_mode (single|chain) and the ordered list of agents that answer it; the assignment rule is stated in the config header and justified per question.
location: research_questions.yaml; report section 6.1 (assignment rule) and the per-question table; application tab 'Research questions' shows the same pairing at runtime.
closed_by: A stated decision rule rather than an assertion: one pass over one table is a single agent; deriving a variable, testing an association and checking the claim against source data is a chain, because the critic step is what keeps unsupported numbers out of the report.

requirement: Prove the dataset size (hundreds of failure records).
evidence: N = 3,089 retained failure records after exclusion; 8 public repositories; 8 frameworks; 2023-2026. Exclusions are counted and stored with a reason per record.
location: failures.jsonl (27 fields); dataset_sources.csv; report section 5; paper Table 1.
closed_by: Per-source record counts with date range, traceback availability and mean body length, so the total can be reconstructed from the table rather than taken on trust.

requirement: Document public dataset sources (Hugging Face, AI-dev datasets, CrewAI/AutoGen/LangGraph, GitHub issues and logs).
evidence: 8 public GitHub repositories across 8 frameworks, with per-source counts, date ranges and traceback coverage. The source-selection rationale is stated, and the corpus is now published as a Hugging Face dataset with a schema, a codebook, a licence and a card that states its limits.
location: dataset_sources.csv; report section 5.1; outputs/hf_dataset/ (dataset card, parquet, codebook); deploy/push_hf.py (publish path); data/raw/ retains the collected payload.
closed_by: A source-selection rationale: issue trackers give a permalink per failure, which is what traceability requires; aggregated datasets do not. The corpus is then released in the format those aggregated datasets use, so a reader can load it the same way and check it row by row.

requirement: Document how the taxonomy and the dataset actually enter the application.
evidence: The taxonomy is loaded from taxonomy.v1.yaml at process start; the dataset is loaded from failures.jsonl (3,089 rows). Both are required arguments to the orchestrator, not hard-coded.
location: taxonomy.py, analysis.py, agents.py; report section 7.1; outputs/app/service/ for the deployed instance.
closed_by: An explicit data-flow: config -> orchestrator -> agent blackboard -> verified result -> table/figure/export. The application refuses to run on a taxonomy that fails validation.

requirement: Architecture showing what every agent does.
evidence: 8 agents on a shared blackboard: Planner, Tagger, Statistician, Causal, Comparator, Complexity, Critic, Exporter. Each declares its goal, its inputs and the functions it may call; the critic can reject a table.
location: agents.py; report section 7.2 with the agent table; application tab 'How it works' streams the same trace live.
closed_by: A per-agent contract table plus a live run trace, so the architecture can be inspected rather than described.

requirement: Statistical results, tables, percentages and visual reports.
evidence: Every question has a table with denominators, Wilson 95% CIs, effect size and corrected p-values; figures are generated from the same verified results object.
location: tables/, figures/, analysis_results.json; report section 8; paper section 4.
closed_by: A verification step that recomputes each headline number from the raw records before it is allowed into a report.

requirement: Tables, percentages and visual reports tied to a research question.
evidence: All 10 questions produce a named primary output; each report subsection states the question it answers in its heading (e.g. '8.5 Framework differences (RQ4)').
location: Report section 8.1-8.11; analysis_report.md.
closed_by: Heading-level mapping between question and result, so no table floats free of a question.

requirement: Report the most common failures as a result tied to a research question.
evidence: RQ1: Functionality / reasoning defect is the largest category at 748 of 3,089 records (24.2%) with a Wilson 95% CI; the full ranking with CIs is reported alongside.
location: Report section 8.1 (RQ1) and 8.2 (RQ2 sensitivity); figure 1.
closed_by: The claim is stated with a denominator, an interval and a stability test (F1) rather than as a bare percentage.

requirement: Main causes of failures, as an explicit root-cause classification rather than only failure categories.
evidence: A second, separate dimension (B) codes cause class with 10 codes; its association with failure type is tested with Cramer's V and BH-corrected p-values. Evidence is graded demonstrated / supported / hypothesised.
location: taxonomy.v1.yaml dimension B; report section 8.4 (RQ3); paper section 4.4.
closed_by: Cause is graded, not assumed: a cause is only called demonstrated when the report names a checkable mechanism. Causal language is suppressed for associations.

requirement: Quantitative comparison of frameworks based on the dataset.
evidence: RQ4 tests the framework x failure-type table (chi-square, Cramer's V); RQ5 compares blocking-severity rates with Wilson CIs and pairwise Fisher tests. Leave-one-framework-out confirms the association is not produced by one repository.
location: Report sections 8.5 and 8.6; leave_one_framework_out.csv.
closed_by: A stated guard: this is a comparison of failure composition, not a quality ranking, because exposure and reporting behaviour differ by project.

requirement: A measurable definition of agent complexity and an analysis if the complexity RQ is retained.
evidence: Index 0-3 = sum of three binary declared capabilities (multi_agent, uses_tools, uses_memory) with fixed lexicons. Tier counts: 0=699, 1=1258, 2=921, 3=211. Each component separately tracks orchestration/context failure (differences multi_agent +16.6pp, uses_tools +3.9pp, uses_memory +20.0pp).
location: complexity.py; complexity_definition.json; report section 8.8; paper section 4.6.
closed_by: The RQ was retained only after the measure was written down as a construct with components, thresholds, known limitations and three quality checks.

requirement: Simple experiments for validation.
evidence: Two experiment suites are reported. Instrument suite E1-E5: reference agreement, perturbation robustness, structural-cue ablation, confidence calibration, second-coder protocol. Finding suite F1-F4: resampling, temporal holdout, leave-one-framework-out, label-noise sensitivity.
location: validation.py, findings_validation.py; report sections 9 and 10; findings_validation.json.
closed_by: The pilot CrewAI/AutoGen repair experiment is cited as prior pilot work, not re-reported as a result of this corpus study. The equivalent role here is played by the E and F suites, which are reproducible from the shipped data.

requirement: Demonstrate how the classification and the results were checked.
evidence: Instrument: exact agreement 51.0% (macro-F1 0.536, kappa 0.44) on n=100; perturbation retention 81.3%. Findings: 5 claims tested - 2 stable, 2 direction-stable, 1 not stable.
location: Report section 9 (instrument) and section 10 (findings); validation_summary.json, findings_validation.json.
closed_by: A validation suite that is allowed to return 'not stable'. The temporal holdout does: composition differs between the early and late corpus, so the headline mix is reported as period-specific and RQ9 is promoted from optional to required.

requirement: Conduct an empirical study establishing a taxonomy of failures in agentic applications and identify their causes.
evidence: N = 3,089 records; 5 dimensions; cause class coded separately and graded.
location: Report sections 4-8; paper sections 3-4.

requirement: The taxonomy classifies different types of failure, e.g. functionality, data structure, tool-related; the first step is to identify all classes.
evidence: 10 failure-type codes including functionality (A1), data structure (A6) and tool-related (A2); classes were identified before being counted, and the identification step is documented.
location: taxonomy.v1.yaml dimension A; report section 4.1.

requirement: After the taxonomy, analyse the causes of each type of failure by exploring the datasets.
evidence: Cause-by-type contingency analysis with Cramer's V, lift per cell and BH correction; evidence grading separates demonstrated mechanisms from hypotheses.
location: Report section 8.4 (RQ3); paper section 4.4.

location: dataset_sources.csv; report section 5; outputs/hf_dataset/; deploy/push_hf.py.
